messages:
rachel: PolarHealth POC - they rotated keys while we were running canaries and now getting 401s across responses + embeddings. Started ~08:42 UTC. Can we swarm?

mike: can you paste curl + response? 401 usually binding/rotation issue or signer mismatch.

rachel: customer sent: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses -H \"Authorization: Bearer ph_live_ABC123\" -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}'` -> `{"error":"unauthorized","message":"invalid credentials"}`. No request-id in body.

olivia: searching logs for token ph_live_ABC123. found request_id=5b9c11. auth service: `warn auth: token_bind_failed token=ph_live_ABC123 err=org_mismatch expected_org=polar token_org=polar`

diego: interesting - token was issued under org slug `polar` but their project canonical org is `polarhealth`. They rotated via the console which created a new token bound to the short slug.

auth-bot: automated: token-rotate event detected key=ph_live_ABC123 rotated_by=rachel@redwood at 2026-03-21T08:40:05Z origin=console.

mike: quick repro: ask them to add header `x-rw-org: polar` or use project header `x-rw-project` with the project's id. Example curl to test: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer ph_live_ABC123\" \
  -H \"x-rw-org: polar\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"input\":\"probe\"}'
```

rachel: sent that. customer replies some infra strips custom headers for Lambda-based functions. They asked if we can create a dual-bound token for the POC. Also asked a security question in their questionnaire: "Can keys be scoped to multiple orgs and projects?"

sec-bot: automated: questionnaire flag noted id=Q-7782 questioner=polarhealth@polarcorp.

olivia: answer for questionnaire: yes, tokens support allowed_orgs and allowed_projects arrays and granular scopes. We recommend creating a short-lived service key scoped to needed endpoints + allowed_orgs for POC. Paste snippet?

diego: paste this snippet into SQA: `service key supports fields: allowed_orgs:["polar","polarhealth"], allowed_projects:["proj_123"], scopes:["generate:basic","embed:read"], ttl:48h; rotate and revoke post-POC.`

auth-bot: automated: policy-check: token ph_live_ABC123 scopes=[generate:basic] required for responses endpoint OK. Logs indicate only org mismatch.

mike: ops option: create service key bound to both org slugs `polar` and `polarhealth` with TTL 48h. Security prefers issuing a new key rather than modifying an existing prod key.

rachel: customer asked whether aliasing the project is feasible so they don't change code. How do we handle aliases?

olivia: we can add an org alias mapping `polar -> polarhealth` or add project alias `polarhealth-staging -> polar`. Aliases require audit + TTL; recommend alias for POC if acceptable to sec.

sec-bot: automated: alias-request queued id=alias-9901 requested_by=rachel@redwood reason="poc-polarhealth temp alias". Approver needed.

diego: while we await approval, create the temporary dual-bound service key and deliver to customer via secure notes. I'll set TTL 72h.

rachel: created key sk_poc_polar_01 with allowed_orgs=["polar","polarhealth"] scopes=["generate:basic","embed:read"] ttl=72h and delivered via secure channel. Customer tested and posted request_id=5b9c12 with HTTP 200.

mike: follow-up: remind customer to rotate and revoke after POC, avoid embedding keys in client apps; for mobile use short-lived backend tokens. Also AE to confirm Dedicated pricing for sustained load.

rachel: AE note added and will hand to @mike for pricing. Closing auth incident. :thumbsup:
